rationale: Request the execution of the completed basis for the Node-wrapper question. The corrected harness now also measures the restore path: after the witness, the wrapped node campaigns and wins (status StateLeader at term 2 with itself as known leader), and the repeated Propose call returns no error in 0ms with its commit index advancing from 5 to 6. The earlier control, premises and witness comparisons are kept, so one receipt covers the whole arc: the channel works before the removal, stays closed after the re-add with the same leader, and re-opens once the leadership changes.

experiment.revision_reason: The harness now also runs the leadership-change restore path after the witness: the wrapped node campaigns on the corrected prefix (its log is consistent, so the election is winnable) and the same Propose call is repeated; the campaign and the repeated call are observed through the node's status channel. The earlier observations are kept.

scope.description: Observe the application-facing proposal path of the Node wrapper for one wrapped node 2 that leader 1 removes from the configuration and then adds back in the same term, with the application duties of the Ready/Advance contract honoured: Propose before the removal, after the re-add, and after the wrapped node wins a leadership change.
assumptions: Two voters {1,2} in one process: node 2 is driven through the Node wrapper (newNodeTestHarness, Readys consumed, entries/hard state persisted, Advance called) while node 1 is a bare raft instance driven by the harness's message pump; node 1 is made leader directly and broadcasts its appends.

Both nodes apply the removal and the re-add through the application path (n1.applyConfChange and the wrapper's ApplyConfChange), and every snapshot of node 2 is taken through its status channel (node.Status), executed inside the run loop.
Propose is called with a 300ms context deadline.
After the witness, the wrapped node campaigns; the harness pumps messages until its status reports StateLeader and then repeats the Propose call, recording the node's commit index before and after.

experiment.prefix: Create the wrapped node 2 over its own storage and a bare node 1 over storages with voters {1,2}; make node 1 leader at term 1 and broadcast its appends; pump messages (persisting whatever node 2's Readys carry) until node 2 knows leader 1 and has applied the bootstrap entry; propose through the wrapper and record the outcome; propose the removal of node 2 on node 1, pump, and apply it on both nodes; propose the re-add of node 2 on node 1, pump, and apply it on both nodes; then propose through the wrapper again and record the outcome and the leader's log index around it. Then the wrapped node campaigns, the harness pumps until it reports StateLeader, and the Propose call is repeated with the node's commit index recorded around it.
experiment.requirement: Node.Propose is the application-facing proposal path: its documentation states that it proposes data to be appended to the log and warns only that proposals can be lost without notice (node.go:138-140). A node that the application has added back to the configuration, and that knows the leader of that configuration, must therefore be able to hand a proposal to raft - or report why it cannot - rather than block until the caller's context expires while the group never sees the proposal.
experiment.responsibility: raft (target): the wrapper's own bookkeeping decides whether the application's proposals reach the group, and the target's comment at node.go:409-411 records that this bookkeeping is unsound.

comparisons.description: Control: while node 2 is a plain member of {1,2} and knows leader 1, Propose returns no error.
Control: the proposal forwarded by the follower reaches the group - the leader's log index is 2 after the call (the bootstrap entry plus this proposal).
Premise on the witness event: the leader's configuration contains node 2 again after the re-add.
Premise on the witness event: the wrapped node still knows leader 1, in the same term, so the leadership is unchanged across the removal and the re-add.
Witness: with node 2 a member again and still knowing leader 1, Propose returns only when its context deadline fires (context deadline exceeded after about 300ms).
Witness: the proposal never reached the group - the leader's log index is unchanged at 4 across the call.
Restore premise: after the campaign the wrapped node reports itself as leader, so r.lead changed from 1 to 2 in the same run.
Restore path: with the leadership changed, Propose returns no error.
Restore path: the proposal reaches the group - the node's commit index advances from 5 to 6.
